body:
WHAT
syncTargets copies the released version into every package.json listed under 'targets' in version.config.json: the root, engine/protocol, engine/providers, engine/core, engine/tools, engine/host, app and tui (eight files). It replaces only the value of the first "version" field with a regex so field order, indentation and line endings stay as they were, and reports for each file the old and new value and whether it changed. A '*' segment in a target path expands to every subdirectory; missing targets are skipped, not errors.

WHY
The VERSION file is the truth but npm and electron-builder read package.json; a manifest left behind ships a build whose parts disagree about what version they are.

WHERE
tools/version/lib/sync.mjs — syncTargets(root, config, next, {dryRun}), writeJsonVersion(root, relative, text, dryRun), expand(root, pattern); version.config.json — 'targets' array of eight paths; called by tools/version/bin/magentra-version.mjs commandApply and reportPlan (dryRun).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Load the real version.config.json and assert config.targets has exactly 8 entries whose paths are package.json, engine/protocol/package.json, engine/providers/package.json, engine/core/package.json, engine/tools/package.json, engine/host/package.json, app/package.json and tui/package.json, and that each file exists in the repo with a string 'version' field.
2. In a temp root that mirrors those eight paths with differing versions, syncTargets(root, config, parse('1.2.3')) returns 8 results, each with to '1.2.3' and changed true, and re-reading every file shows JSON.parse(...).version === '1.2.3'.
3. A target file written with 4-space indent, CRLF line endings and 'version' as the third key keeps its byte layout except the version value (compare against the original with only that substring replaced); a second run reports changed false and writes nothing (mtime unchanged).
4. With dryRun:true the returned results show from/to and changed:true but no file on disk changes; a target path that does not exist is skipped without an error; a target that is not valid JSON throws an error naming the file; a JSON file without a 'version' field yields no result entry.
5. A config target 'pkgs/*/package.json' with directories pkgs/a, pkgs/b and pkgs/.hidden expands to a and b only, in sorted order.
